import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Mathoverflow 347178

*Reference:* [mathoverflow/347178](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/347178)
asked by user [*Biagio Ricceri*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/149235/biagio-ricceri)
-/

open Real Set
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Mathoverflow347178

/--
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Is it true that
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x) = \sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$$?

Answer: No. A counterexample in $\mathbb R^2$ is recorded in the linked formal proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 26,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/fc20c0b55eab6fc26e2bb5b24fb3005303a0910b"]
theorem mathoverflow_347178 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 f),
        (BddAbove (range f) ↔ BddAbove (range (fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)))) ∧
        (⨆ x, (f x : EReal)) = ⨆ x, (f (x + gradient f x) : EReal) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Is the boundedness of
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x)$ and $\sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$ equivalent?

Answer: No. The same counterexample is recorded in the linked formal proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 26,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/fc20c0b55eab6fc26e2bb5b24fb3005303a0910b"]
theorem mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_iff :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 f),
        BddAbove (range f) ↔ BddAbove (range fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Does the equality
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x) = \sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$$
hold when both suprema are finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 26]
theorem mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_only :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
        (h : BddAbove (range f)) (h' : BddAbove (range (fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)))),
        (⨆ x, f x) = ⨆ x, f (x + gradient f x) := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow347178

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement conjoins equivalence of boundedness above with equality of the EReal suprema; the original question asks only for equality of the suprema.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any real-valued function f, BddAbove (range f) is equivalent to (⨆ x, (f x : EReal)) < ⊤. Consequently, equality of the two extended-real suprema implies the boundedness equivalence, making the extra conjunct redundant. The full quantified equivalence, including an arbitrary answer proposition, was proved as Review347178.main_reformulation in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses real-valued suprema and explicitly assumes boundedness above of both ranges. The source’s answer discusses the variant under the single condition sup f < ∞.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing T(x)=x+∇f(x), range (f ∘ T) is contained in range f, so the second boundedness hypothesis follows from the first. Both domains are nonempty, so their ranges have genuine real suprema under these hypotheses, and coercing those suprema to EReal preserves them. Thus the Lean statement is equivalent to equality of extended-real suprema assuming only sup f < ⊤. The full quantified equivalence was proved as Review347178.bounded_reformulation in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical defects found in the three declarations. The MathOverflow answer records a C¹ counterexample in dimension 2 with sup f = +∞ and sup f(x+∇f(x)) = 0, agreeing with both solved/False records. It leaves the general finite-supremum variant unresolved. Lean checks verified quantifier and answer scope, the negative-answer polarity, genuine gradients under C¹, nonempty ranges, constant-function boundary cases, and the Real/EReal supremum conventions. The equivalence and polarity proofs compile with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, without using the target theorems’ sorry axioms. The reviewed file was not modified.
